checks.description: Security group ingress rules must not allow SSH (port 22) from the public internet (0.0.0.0/0). TFSEC LIMITATION: This check applies to all aws_security_group_rule resources with type=ingress and flags any rule that allows unrestricted IPv4 access. Rules for intentionally public ports (80, 443) should carry a tfsec-ignore:CALIPER-AWS-007 annotation. For port-specific conditional enforcement, use OPA/Sentinel or tfsec built-in rule aws-vpc-no-public-ingress-sgr.
checks.impact: Allowing SSH ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 exposes instances to brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks from the entire internet, bypassing network-level access controls
checks.resolution: Replace 0.0.0.0/0 in cidr_blocks with a specific CIDR range (bastion host IP, VPN CIDR, or management subnet). Use a bastion host or AWS Systems Manager Session Manager instead of direct SSH exposure
checks.errorMessage: Security group rule allows unrestricted IPv4 ingress (0.0.0.0/0). SSH and other management ports must restrict access to known IP ranges

checks.description: Security group ingress rules must not allow SSH (port 22) from the public internet (::/0 IPv6). TFSEC LIMITATION: This check applies to all aws_security_group_rule resources and flags any rule that allows unrestricted IPv6 access. Rules for intentionally public ports (80, 443) should carry a tfsec-ignore:CALIPER-AWS-007-IPV6 annotation.
checks.impact: Allowing SSH ingress from ::/0 exposes dual-stack instances to brute-force attacks over IPv6, a path often overlooked in security group reviews
checks.resolution: Replace ::/0 in ipv6_cidr_blocks with a specific IPv6 CIDR range, or remove IPv6 ingress on management ports entirely
checks.errorMessage: Security group rule allows unrestricted IPv6 ingress (::/0). SSH and other management ports must restrict access to known IPv6 ranges
